content: Periodontal disease occurs more frequently and tends to be more severe in individuals with diabetes compared to those who do not have diabetes. Elevated A1C levels, which indicate poorer glycemic control, are linked to a higher likelihood of developing periodontal disease as well as increased severity of the condition. Although certain studies suggest that treating periodontal disease might lead to improvements in diabetes management and outcomes, the overall effect of such treatment on diabetes remains a subject of ongoing debate and is not yet definitively established.
